# harmoniq_instance_setting (Resource)

An instance setting kept in the registry's database, over the environment's defaults (INST-34). Needs an instance API key (`hq_inst_…`, scope `instance:admin`). Destroying it resets the setting to the environment's defaults. A change made elsewhere (the admin panel, an import) shows as a diff and the next apply restores this value.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Instance administration uses an instance API key (hq_inst_…, scope instance:admin),
# created by an instance owner in the admin panel.
provider "harmoniq" {
  alias   = "instance"
  api_key = var.harmoniq_instance_api_key
}

resource "harmoniq_instance_setting" "gc" {
  provider = harmoniq.instance
  key      = "gc"
  value = jsonencode({
    keepVersions         = 20
    defaultRetentionDays = 90
  })
}

resource "harmoniq_instance_setting" "branding" {
  provider = harmoniq.instance
  key      = "branding"
  value = jsonencode({
    name       = "Acme Frontends"
    supportUrl = "https://help.acme.example"
  })
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `key` (String) `storage`, `email`, `auth`, `branding`, `tenancy`, `plans`, `rateLimits`, `gc` or `bundles`.
- `value` (String, Sensitive) The setting as JSON, usually `jsonencode({...})`; see the registry's API reference for each key. Secrets (SMTP password, storage keys) are write-only.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The setting key.
- `version` (Number) The setting's saved version (INST-35).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import harmoniq_instance_setting.gc gc
```
